headline: Common Mistakes to Avoid After a Rear-End Collision
articleBody: Getting hit from behind can be a real shocker, and in the aftermath, it's easy to make a few missteps that could actually harm your future claim. Understanding these common mistakes can save you a lot of headache and protect your rights. One big no-no is not calling the police. Even if the damage seems minor, a police report creates an official record of the incident, which is super helpful for insurance claims later. Another mistake is forgetting to gather evidence. Snap photos of everything – the damage to both cars, the scene itself, skid marks, and any visible injuries. Exchange insurance and contact info with the other driver, and get names and numbers of any witnesses too. Don't, I repeat, don't admit fault or apologize, even if you feel a little shaken. Anything you say can be used against you, and the full picture of what happened might not be clear yet. A lot of people also mistakenly delay seeking medical attention. Some injuries, especially whiplash, might not manifest until days later. See a doctor promptly, even if you feel fine, to document any potential injuries. Finally, don't rush into accepting a quick settlement offer from the insurance company without understanding the full extent of your damages. Their first offer is rarely their best. If you're feeling pressured or unsure about any of these steps, remember that a seasoned attorney, someone like Brett Peterson, can guide you through the process and ensure you don't compromise your right to fair compensation.
